sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Radioligand binding ([3H]-MLT and 2-[125I]-MLT) to crude membranes from HEK293 cells expressing HA-tagged GPR61 was comparable to untagged receptor, confirming preserved ligand-binding function.
sites.rationale: GPR61 has no signal peptide in the computed topology; residues 1–43 form the sole extracellular N-terminal domain, making position 0 (prepend before M1) the unique extracellular terminus for an N-terminal tag. L1–L5 collectively document HA-tag addition at the amino-terminal extremity of full-length, membrane-anchored GPR61. L2 confirms surface display on intact cells and L3 confirms ligand-binding function is preserved, yielding the highest validation level. The 43-residue extracellular N-terminus provides ample space for a short epitope tag well clear of TM1 (which begins at residue 44). Full-length GPR61 with HA tag (YPYDVPDYA) added by PCR at the amino-terminal extremity, inserted into pcDNA3 and expressed in HEK293T cells. The topology shows residues 1–43 as extracellular with no signal peptide, so the tag prepends before residue 1 (the sole extracellular terminus). Surface display confirmed by confocal microscopy on intact (non-permeabilized) HEK293T cells with anti-HA antibodies.

sources.claim: ( C , D ) Binding of [ 3 H]-MLT ( C ) and 2-[ 125 I]-MLT ( D ) to crude membrane prepared from HEK293 cells expressing HA-tagged or untagged GPR61, GPR62 or GPR135.

literature_notes: L6–L8 (C-terminal Myc tag) and L10 (C-terminal FLAG tag) were considered but the C-terminus of GPR61 (residues 345–451) is entirely intracellular per the computed topology; these are intracellular tags and do not qualify as surface sites. L9 (BRIL insertion in ICL3 between R233 and K285) is an intracellular insertion (ICL3 = residues 230–287) used for structural studies; it does not qualify. L10 also mentions an HA signal peptide at the N-terminus of the structural construct, but this is a heterologous signal peptide used for trafficking, not a tag on the receptor surface. L11 describes a heavily engineered active-conformation structural construct (HA-SP + FLAG + TEV + BRIL + PreScission + GPR61 N-terminus + C-terminal Gαs fusion); the FLAG tag is at the extracellular N-terminus of GPR61 in a full-length membrane-anchored context, which corroborates the N-terminal tagging site already established by L1–L5, but L11 is not used as the primary supporting clip because L3 provides stronger functional validation with a simpler construct. The 6myc-GPR61-PK2 construct mentioned in L5 also places a 6myc tag at the N-terminus (extracellular), further corroborating the site, but again L3 is the primary anchor.
